Manager test finding for task 1 of LectorIA-meta. `gitleaks dir . --redact` (gitleaks 8.28, at ~/.local/bin/gitleaks) reports `generic-api-key` on the placeholder `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY=xxx-replace-me-1234567890` in `scripts/check-secrets.test.mjs` line ~99, and on the same string echoed in `agent-logs/*.jsonl` session logs. The pre-commit hook runs `gitleaks git --staged`, so these files cannot be committed.
Fix with the smallest change: add a `.gitleaks.toml` at the repo root that extends the default config (`[extend] useDefault = true`) and allowlists only these known test placeholders by regex (e.g. strings containing `xxx-replace-me`, `your-key-here`, `changeme-please`, `paste-your-salt-here`), not whole paths. Do not allowlist `agent-logs/` as a path: session logs must still be scanned for real keys. Verify with `gitleaks dir . --redact --no-banner` (expect no leaks) and `npm run test:hooks`. Mention `.gitleaks.toml` in one line in SECURITY.md where gitleaks is described. Do not commit. End with a short summary.

1|# Security
2|
3|## Report a vulnerability
4|
5|Use GitHub private vulnerability reporting on this repo. Do not open a public issue for a security bug.
6|
7|## What is in place now
8|
9|- Secrets live only in env vars. `.env.example` holds names, never values.
10|- A pre-commit scan blocks staged secrets: gitleaks when installed, plus the built-in scanner in `scripts/check-secrets.mjs`, which always runs.
11|- GitHub secret scanning and push protection guard the remote.
12|- Dependabot alerts track vulnerable dependencies.
13|
14|## Rules for later tasks
15|
16|Planned, not built yet. Each app task implements its share.
17|
18|- The BYOK Meta key is never stored server-side or in logs. It stays in the browser session (`sessionStorage`) and travels over HTTPS per request in a header.
19|- The anonymous session cookie is signed with HMAC (`SESSION_SECRET`) and set httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax.
20|- IPs are stored only as salted hashes (`IP_HASH_SALT`) with daily keys.
21|- Quotas are strict per person: 15 questions and 5 images per day, counted by hashed IP and anonymous cookie, whichever runs out first. A global spend cap in Redis sits above them.
22|- Turnstile runs once per session.
23|- Errors never return stack traces or raw exception text.
24|- Book source files (epub, raw text) are never publicly served. Only processed public-domain JSON leaves the server.
25|- Security headers and a CSP live in `next.config.ts`.
26|- Input limits hold: question 500 chars, passage 600 chars. The server verifies each passage against the book text.
